irExtensionCandidates.sourceEvidence: §1.01 (Consolidated Net Income) clauses (2),(4),(7)-(10),(12)-(17),(19) and the closing addback paragraph
irExtensionCandidates.semanticRequirement: A recurring pattern across EBITDA/Net-Income style definitions: a named, well-understood categorical accounting adjustment (e.g. 'non-cash equity compensation expense', 'mark-to-market movement under ASC 815') that is real, fully identified by the drafters, and has clear semantic meaning, but carries no fixed numeric value in the contract text itself because its magnitude depends on the specific Person's actual financial results for the period in question.
irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: Existing arithmetic/reference primitives (MONEY, PERCENT, METRIC_REFERENCE, etc.) all presuppose either a literal contractual value or a named external metric that is itself independently defined/reportable (like 'Consolidated EBITDA'). These categorical adjustment clauses are neither - they are ad hoc, period-specific accounting line items with no separate defined-term status and no stated formula value, so representing them with METRIC_REFERENCE would falsely imply they are independently defined/reportable metrics, while UNSUPPORTED (the safe current choice) discards the fact that these are fully-understood, well-scoped, real components of the calculation rather than genuinely indeterminate content.
irExtensionCandidates.candidateGeneralizedPrimitive: CATEGORICAL_ADJUSTMENT node (semanticDescription, direction: ADD|SUBTRACT, sourceStandardRef) - a typed placeholder representing a real, named but numerically unquantified GAAP/accounting adjustment category, distinguishable in downstream tooling from a true UNSUPPORTED/unrepresentable gap.

This submission compiles solely the definition of "Consolidated Net Income" at §1.01. No independently operative WireRule exists within this definitional text (no rules array populated) - the provision is purely a defined-term calculation.

Phase 2's own gathered context repeatedly shows a closely parallel sibling definition, "Consolidated Maintenance Net Income", with materially identical exclusion/addback structure; that sibling term was not requested for separate compilation because it is a distinct defined term outside the specific provision assigned (Consolidated Net Income) and is preserved only as background evidence, not compiled here.

The $5,000,000 cap in clause (11) is the only clause bearing a literal, fixed dollar figure in the entire definition; it is represented with a genuine MONEY node inside a MIN capping structure rather than folded into an UNSUPPORTED description, consistent with the CRITICAL threshold item in the frozen inventory.

All 61 frozen inventory items were either consumed on a specific IR node (with matching value/meaning) or dispositioned as INTENTIONALLY_NON_COMPUTATIONAL (the four reserved clauses); none were silently omitted.

definitions.excerpt: "Consolidated Net Income" means, with respect to any Person for any period, the net income (loss) of such Person and its Subsidiaries for such period determined on a consolidated basis in accordance with GAAP, excluding (and excluding the effect of), without duplication, ... [clauses (1)-(20)] ... In addition, ... Consolidated Net Income will include the amount of proceeds received or receivable from business interruption insurance ...
sufficiencyReasons: Overall structure (base GAAP consolidated net income/loss, sequential without-duplication exclusions under clauses (2),(4)-(19), and the final addback for insurance/reimbursement/indemnification amounts) is fully captured compositionally.

Most individual exclusion/inclusion categories are categorical GAAP/accounting adjustments with no fixed dollar value stated in the source text (their actual amount depends on the Person's real financial statements); these are faithfully represented as UNSUPPORTED nodes carrying their full descriptive content, conditions, alternatives and citations rather than a fabricated numeric formula.

The one genuine fixed numeric component in the definition - the $5,000,000 aggregate cap (clause (11) proviso) on charges/nonrecurring merger costs from unsuccessful or non-consummated transactions - is fully represented with a real MONEY node inside a MIN capping structure.

Two internal cross-references ('permitted under this Agreement' in clause (13); 'permitted hereunder' in the addback paragraph) do not identify a specific section; preserved as-is rather than guessed at a target section.

irExtensionCandidates.sourceEvidence: §1.01 (Consolidated Net Income) clauses (2),(4),(7)-(10),(12)-(17),(19) and the closing addback paragraph
irExtensionCandidates.semanticRequirement: A recurring pattern across EBITDA/Net-Income style definitions: a named, well-understood categorical accounting adjustment (e.g. 'non-cash equity compensation expense', 'mark-to-market movement under ASC 815') that is real, fully identified by the drafters, and has clear semantic meaning, but carries no fixed numeric value in the contract text itself because its magnitude depends on the specific Person's actual financial results for the period in question.
irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: Existing arithmetic/reference primitives (MONEY, PERCENT, METRIC_REFERENCE, etc.) all presuppose either a literal contractual value or a named external metric that is itself independently defined/reportable (like 'Consolidated EBITDA'). These categorical adjustment clauses are neither - they are ad hoc, period-specific accounting line items with no separate defined-term status and no stated formula value, so representing them with METRIC_REFERENCE would falsely imply they are independently defined/reportable metrics, while UNSUPPORTED (the safe current choice) discards the fact that these are fully-understood, well-scoped, real components of the calculation rather than genuinely indeterminate content.
irExtensionCandidates.candidateGeneralizedPrimitive: CATEGORICAL_ADJUSTMENT node (semanticDescription, direction: ADD|SUBTRACT, sourceStandardRef) - a typed placeholder representing a real, named but numerically unquantified GAAP/accounting adjustment category, distinguishable in downstream tooling from a true UNSUPPORTED/unrepresentable gap.

overallNotes: This submission compiles solely the definition of "Consolidated Net Income" at §1.01. No independently operative WireRule exists within this definitional text (no rules array populated) - the provision is purely a defined-term calculation.

Phase 2's own gathered context repeatedly shows a closely parallel sibling definition, "Consolidated Maintenance Net Income", with materially identical exclusion/addback structure; that sibling term was not requested for separate compilation because it is a distinct defined term outside the specific provision assigned (Consolidated Net Income) and is preserved only as background evidence, not compiled here.

The $5,000,000 cap in clause (11) is the only clause bearing a literal, fixed dollar figure in the entire definition; it is represented with a genuine MONEY node inside a MIN capping structure rather than folded into an UNSUPPORTED description, consistent with the CRITICAL threshold item in the frozen inventory.

All 61 frozen inventory items were either consumed on a specific IR node (with matching value/meaning) or dispositioned as INTENTIONALLY_NON_COMPUTATIONAL (the four reserved clauses); none were silently omitted.

findings.sourceEvidence: any charges or nonrecurring merger costs incurred during such period as a result of any such transaction, in each case whether or not successful or consummated (including, for the avoidance of doubt, the effects of expensing all transaction related expenses in accordance with Accounting Standards Codification Topic No. 805, Business Combinations); provided that the amount of charges or nonrecurring merger costs incurred during such period as a result of any such transaction that is not successful or consummated shall not exceed $5,000,000 in the aggregate
findings.proposedIrEvidence: Operand 1 (uncapped, ir-expr:ad24cf7cd74a8e5808fc2132) semanticDescription: '...whether consummated before, on or after the Closing Date, whether completed or not, including related nonrecurring merger costs regardless of success, including the effect of expensing transaction-related expenses under ASC Topic No. 805.' Operand 2 (ir-expr:097284472677f914c24b0003) is MIN(TRANSACTION_INPUT_REFERENCE 'Aggregate Charges or Nonrecurring Merger Costs from Unsuccessful or Non-Consummated Transactions During the Period', $5,000,000).
findings.verifierReasoning: The source proviso caps only the specific sub-category of 'charges or nonrecurring merger costs...as a result of any such transaction that is not successful or consummated' at $5,000,000 in the aggregate; all other fees/expenses/charges (including merger costs from successful transactions) are uncapped. The proposed IR splits clause (11) into an uncapped operand and a separately capped operand, which is the right general shape, but the uncapped operand's own semanticDescription explicitly states it includes 'related nonrecurring merger costs regardless of success' - i.e., the same 'unsuccessful/non-consummated transaction merger costs' category that operand 2 is supposed to cap. As drafted, the same dollar amount could be counted once in the uncapped bucket and again (redundantly) in the capped bucket, which would functionally nullify or double-count the $5,000,000 cap rather than faithfully applying it only to the unsuccessful-transaction subset as the source requires. This is a genuine formula-shape/grouping defect, not merely an honest disclosure of missing data, because the overlap is asserted affirmatively in the operand-1 description rather than left open.

findings.sourceEvidence: "Consolidated Net Income” means, with respect to any Person for any period, the net income (loss) of such Person and its Subsidiaries for such period determined on a consolidated basis in accordance with GAAP...
findings.verifierReasoning: The source definition is a generic function parameterized over 'any Person' and 'any period' - it is used throughout the credit agreement to compute Consolidated Net Income for different Persons in different contexts (e.g., the Borrower, a Subsidiary, or an Unrestricted Subsidiary), not for one fixed entity. The proposed IR instead hardcodes the base Net Income metric reference to a single companyId and a single instrumentKey. If this binding is carried forward wherever 'Consolidated Net Income' is invoked for a Person other than the one hardcoded, the resulting calculation would not correspond to the actual Person intended by the operative covenant that cross-references this definition. I cannot fully resolve from the evidence given whether this binding is a benign artifact of the compilation pipeline (e.g., a per-deal default) or an actual scope error, so I am flagging it as uncertain rather than a confirmed defect.
